pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour for the curator, the packers and support. Read it once; the monthly cycle page is the calendar you work to.

Curate the next box: taste samples, pick the lineup, link each item to the edition.
Lock the lineup on the lock date and send the sourcing orders. Units needed is the expected box count plus 3 percent for damages.

text.text: Five or six items, one hero item everyone will talk about.
A balance: something sweet, something savoury, a drink, a pantry item.
Retail value at least 1.5 times the box price. The edition shows cost and value per box; aim for cost under 45 percent of the price.
Allergens checked: every item's allergens on its row, so support can swap items for subscribers who avoid them.
Best-by dates at least three months after ship day.
Link each item to the edition. The lineup count on the edition updates.

Read every reply to the shipping email. A hero item people loved is a candidate for the add-on shop. An item many disliked should not come back, and tells the curator something for next time.
Every subscriber who stays one more month is worth more than a new one, because you have already paid to find them.

Churn is the share of subscribers who leave in a month. Count cancellations this month and divide by active subscribers at the start of the month. A box at 8 percent a month keeps a subscriber about a year; at 5 percent, nearly two years. Look at the
chart on the Dashboard every month.
Failed charges are churn you did not choose
Many cancellations are not decisions: a card expired. Work
First failure: an automatic retry in three days and a friendly email with a link to update the card.
Second failure: a personal email from support. Keep the box queued for now.
Third failure: hold the box, set the subscriber to
, and send one last note. If nothing comes back in a week, cancel with a door left open.
Offer a pause before a cancel

When someone asks to cancel, offer a pause of one, two or three months first, with no fee. Log it on the pause or cancel form. Many pausers come back on their own; send a short email a week before the pause ends showing what is in the next box.
